# Keep-warm coverage

<!-- Generated by tests/keep-warm-matrix.test.ts; do not edit. `CACHE_KEEPER_MATRIX=update npm test` writes it again; `npm test` fails while it is out of date. -->

Who keeps an idle cache warm, for every model in the catalog of pi-ai 1.6.0 (1,698 models of 42 providers), as the sweep in `tests/keep-warm-matrix.test.ts` finds it: 12,632 combinations of

- cache retention `short` and `long` (`PI_CACHE_RETENTION`, as the extension sets it);
- model data: Pi's catalog only, or a cache lifetime for both tiers as providers.dev would supply it (the extension writes one only for a tier the catalog has none for; the sweep uses 300 s and 3,600 s, so this shows the extension's behaviour with data, not the data);
- thinking off, and `high` where the model has it.

Each request is built by pi's own adapter for the model's API, with a system prompt, one tool and one user message, and passes through the extension as Pi sends it. Its answer reads the cached prompt and writes a little, reporting the 1-hour share of the write where pi's adapter reports one (Anthropic Messages, Bedrock). Keep-warm is on for 2 hours. "Kept warm" means the extension owns the idle period (Pi's own idle warming is told to stop) and sends one capped refresh before the cache expires; "Pi" means it is left to Pi's own warming and the extension sends nothing.

## Totals

| Retention, model data | Combinations | Kept warm (lifetimes) | Left to Pi |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| short, Pi's catalog | 3,158 | 551 (5 min, 30 min) | 2,607 |
| short, with lifetimes | 3,158 | 1,996 (5 min) | 1,162 |
| long, Pi's catalog | 3,158 | 543 (5 min, 30 min, 1 h) | 2,615 |
| long, with lifetimes | 3,158 | 1,968 (5 min, 1 h) | 1,190 |
| all | 12,632 | 5,058 | 7,574 |

A period the extension keeps warm always sends its refresh: where the model's prices make one refresh cost at least as much as the cache miss it would avoid (a cached read priced like an uncached one, or no discount at all), the period is left to Pi (*refresh costs a miss*).

## Left to Pi, by reason

| Reason (as `/cache-keeper` says it) | short, Pi's catalog | short, with lifetimes | long, Pi's catalog | long, with lifetimes | All |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| the cache lifetime is unknown (*no lifetime*) | 1,932 | 0 | 1,932 | 0 | 3,864 |
| this API's requests are not re-sent by the extension (*API not re-sent*) | 392 | 710 | 392 | 710 | 2,204 |
| the request turns thinking on (thinking: { type: "enabled" }), which a refresh capped at one output token cannot re-send as it was (*thinking enabled*) | 268 | 306 | 268 | 306 | 1,148 |
| at this model's prices a refresh costs as much as a miss (*refresh costs a miss*) | 15 | 146 | 15 | 146 | 322 |
| the request's cache lifetime does not match the model data (*stated lifetime ≠ data*) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 20 | 20 |
| the request carries more than one cache lifetime (*two lifetimes*) | 0 | 0 | 8 | 8 | 16 |

## Routes whose tiers last otherwise

The 4,896 combinations of the three APIs the extension re-sends (`anthropic-messages`, `openai-completions`, `openai-responses`; on every other API a period is Pi's whatever the data) on two more routes, with the lifetimes written as providers.dev would write them (only for a tier the catalog has none for, so Pi's catalog wins where it has one): *short tier 1 h* (3600 s and 3,600 s, as a subscription login serves Claude; its answers report the 1-hour write for any marker) and *long tier 30 min* (300 s and 1,800 s; its answers report the bucket the markers name). A request's lifetime is the one a marker states, else the route's for the tier asked; a write bucket an answer reports is evidence of a lifetime, and a period is kept warm only where it agrees.

| Retention, route | Combinations | Kept warm (lifetimes) | Left to Pi |

| short, short tier 1 h | 2,448 | 1,934 (1 h) | 514 |
| long, short tier 1 h | 2,448 | 1,968 (1 h) | 480 |
| short, long tier 30 min | 2,448 | 1,996 (5 min) | 452 |
| long, long tier 30 min | 2,448 | 1,475 (5 min, 30 min, 1 h) | 973 |
